# Agent controls

<!-- Generated by `obaaf docs build` from src/obaaf/data/. Do not edit by hand. -->

*Generated for OBAAF 0.2, in active adoption with pilot teams. The content may change in OBAAF 0.3 based on pilot feedback; open design decisions are tracked in [DECISIONS.md](../DECISIONS.md).*

Version 0.1.0 (released). Source: Paper 1, sections 5–7 ([*Untrusted Text, Trusted Tokens*](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23622566)). These controls let a team connect AI agents to its build pipeline without lending them the pipeline's authority. They are not specific to games.

## The principle: taint-bounded authority

Every capability an agent invocation can exercise must be one its least-trusted influencer could exercise directly. Adding text to an agent's context must never add authority.

```latex
\forall c \in A(\alpha):\quad \mathrm{req}(c) \sqsubseteq I(\alpha) = \bigsqcap_{p \in \mathit{Inf}(\alpha)} \ell(p)
```

Here *A*(α) is every capability reachable from the agent invocation α, req(*c*) is the lowest trust level allowed to cause capability *c*, and *I*(α) is the level of the least-trusted principal able to influence anything α reads.

## Trust levels

| Level | Typical capabilities at this level |
| --- | --- |
| Public | Comment on a public issue; open a pull request from a fork |
| Contributor | Push to a non-protected branch; apply labels |
| Maintainer | Merge to a protected branch; edit workflow or agent-instruction files; read repository secrets |
| Release | Approve or publish a release; use a signing key |

The levels form a chain: Public ⊑ Contributor ⊑ Maintainer ⊑ Release.

## Lanes

Three lanes and an attestation step (Paper 1, section 7.1), each a separate job with its own identity.

| Lane or step | Runs at | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agent | The integrity level of its inputs (Public for a public repository) | Triggered by issue, comment, or pull-request events. A deterministic snapshot step runs first and records the digests and integrity level of the inputs. The agent then runs on a fresh runner with a read-only token, no secrets, no permission to request OIDC tokens, and egress limited to an inference proxy that holds the model credential. Its instruction files come from the protected base branch. Its only output is a proposal bundle. |
| Attestation step | - (a separate job the agent cannot influence) | Computes the digest of the proposal bundle and signs the agent-run attestation with the platform's OIDC identity. |
| Effect | Maintainer | Triggered when the agent lane completes, behind a protected environment whose required reviewers must approve. Verifies the attestation and the proposal digest, applies deterministic checks, and applies the proposal under its own identity. It never runs the model. |
| Release | Release | Agents do not change it. It builds only from protected branches and, before publishing, verifies that every agent-authored commit in the release range carries an attestation and an approval record. |

The [GitHub Actions templates](../templates/github-actions/README.md) implement these lanes, with two gaps in version 0.1: the agent's egress is declared but enforced only with an egress monitor or a network policy, and the inference proxy is specified but not built yet ([inference proxy](../docs/inference-proxy.md)).

### R1 Label inputs by provenance and bind the snapshot

**Requirement.** Every channel through which content can reach an agent is labeled with the lowest level among the principals able to influence it, and unknown channels are labeled Public. The content an invocation will read is captured when authority is decided, recorded by cryptographic digest, and delivered to the agent from that snapshot. Content fetched during the run is labeled Public unless it comes from a source pinned in advance.

**Why.** R1 makes Inf(α) computable and closes the time-of-check-to-time-of-use gap exploited in the Claude Code action case.

**Root causes.** RC1. **Assumption secured** (Paper 1, Table 2): (ii) sound labeling. **Illustrative cases.** Claude Code action, PromptPwnd.

**On GitHub Actions.** Native: Event payloads identify authors; workflows can be split by trust. Gap and compensating control: No provenance labels or snapshot binding; implement as a deterministic step before the agent.

**New relative to existing standards.** Trust labels for content an automated actor reads.

**In this repository.** Tools: `obaaf snapshot` · Templates: `obaaf-agent-propose.yml: snapshot job` · Checker rules: `OBAAF-GHA-010`

### R2 Derive authority from labels

**Requirement.** Token permissions, secrets, tool sets, and network policy are derived from the invocation's integrity level and fixed when the job starts. An invocation at Public level receives read-only access to public content, no secrets, no write access to protected refs or instruction files, and no general network egress. Reads of private source and secrets are treated as capabilities, so they are withheld from any invocation that untrusted text can steer.

**Why.** R2 is the principle itself, applied at the pipeline layer.

**Root causes.** RC1, RC2. **Assumption secured** (Paper 1, Table 2): The principle itself. **Illustrative cases.** GitHub MCP, GitLab Duo, CamoLeak.

**On GitHub Actions.** Native: Job-level permissions; environment secrets released only after approval. Gap and compensating control: No policy engine maps labels to permissions; enforce through lane structure and organization policy.

**New relative to existing standards.** Labels determine permissions.

**In this repository.** Templates: `obaaf-agent-propose.yml: agent job permissions` · Checker rules: `OBAAF-GHA-003`, `OBAAF-GHA-005`

### R3 Give each invocation its own short-lived identity

**Requirement.** Each invocation authenticates as a workload identity distinct from human users and from other workflows, with credentials issued per job, scoped to one repository and purpose, and expiring when the job ends, as with per-job OIDC-federated credentials. Long-lived personal access tokens are not used. Credentials for the model API are held by a proxy outside the agent's reach, or are short-lived and budget-limited. Calls to downstream services use tokens issued for those services, through token exchange with audience restriction; a token issued for one service is never passed through to another.

**Why.** R3 removes standing authority that the task does not need, and supports assumption (i).

**Root causes.** RC2. **Assumption secured** (Paper 1, Table 2): (i) complete mediation. **Illustrative cases.** PromptPwnd, Amazon Q, Nx.

**On GitHub Actions.** Native: Job tokens that expire with the job; per-job OIDC tokens with claims. Gap and compensating control: Cloud trust policies must constrain the claims; model keys need a proxy.

**New relative to existing standards.** A distinct identity per agent invocation.

**In this repository.** Docs: `docs/inference-proxy.md` · Checker rules: `OBAAF-GHA-004`, `OBAAF-GHA-005`

### R4 Separate proposals from effects

**Requirement.** Any agent output that would change protected state (protected branches, workflow and instruction files, releases, secrets, repository settings) is a proposal. A separate deterministic job applies it, under a different identity, only after policy checks pass and a principal at the required level, other than the requester, approves.

**Why.** R4 is the certified endorsement of Paper 1, section 5.5.

**Root causes.** RC2. **Assumption secured** (Paper 1, Table 2): Certified endorsement. **Illustrative cases.** Nx, Amazon Q.

**On GitHub Actions.** Native: Environments with required reviewers and self-review prevention; branch rulesets. Gap and compensating control: Deterministic checks on proposals are project-defined.

**New relative to existing standards.** Approval of agent proposals by someone other than the requester.

**In this repository.** Tools: `obaaf proposal check`, `obaaf attest approval` · Templates: `obaaf-agent-apply.yml` · Checker rules: `OBAAF-GHA-003`, `OBAAF-GHA-021`, `OBAAF-GHA-022`

### R5 Protect the instruction plane

**Requirement.** Files that steer agents (system prompts, agent instruction files, rules files, tool allow-lists, MCP configurations, and the workflow files that invoke agents) are code. They live on protected branches under code-owner review, are scanned for hidden characters, and are loaded from the protected base branch rather than from the change under review. Agents cannot modify them.

**Why.** Poisoned instructions persist across runs and were the vector in two cases.

**Root causes.** RC1, RC3. **Assumption secured** (Paper 1, Table 2): (ii) sound labeling. **Illustrative cases.** Rules File Backdoor, Amazon Q.

**On GitHub Actions.** Native: Code owners and branch rulesets; push rulesets that restrict file paths, on paid plans for private repositories. Gap and compensating control: Hidden-character scanning is project-defined, though GitHub now warns about hidden Unicode.

**New relative to existing standards.** Agent instruction files treated as code.

**In this repository.** Tools: `obaaf check (instruction-file scan)`, `obaaf proposal check` · Templates: `CODEOWNERS.example`, `obaaf-agent-propose.yml: instructions from the base branch` · Checker rules: `OBAAF-INS-001`, `OBAAF-REPO-001`, `OBAAF-REPO-002`, `OBAAF-GHA-012`

### R6 Verify tools and models as supply chain inputs

**Requirement.** Agent actions, harnesses, containers, and MCP servers are pinned by immutable digest and verified against their provenance where it exists. Tool descriptions and outputs from servers not verified at Maintainer level are labeled Public under R1.

**Why.** A pipeline's trusted components were the vector in the tj-actions compromise.

**Root causes.** RC1. **Assumption secured** (Paper 1, Table 2): (ii) sound labeling. **Illustrative cases.** tj-actions (non-agent).

**On GitHub Actions.** Native: Referencing actions by full commit digest. Gap and compensating control: No native verification of an action's provenance when it is consumed.

**New relative to existing standards.** Tool descriptions treated as untrusted input.

**In this repository.** Checker rules: `OBAAF-GHA-008`

### R7 Isolate the run and constrain egress

**Requirement.** Each invocation runs in a fresh, isolated environment. That environment shares no writable state, including caches, with release jobs, and cannot reach cloud metadata endpoints or container sockets. Network egress is denied by default, except to the model endpoint and to pinned package sources the task requires.

**Why.** R7 removes ambient authority, supporting assumption (i). A cache shared with release jobs turned a triage run into a release compromise in the Cline case, and unexpected egress is how the tj-actions compromise was first detected.

**Root causes.** RC2. **Assumption secured** (Paper 1, Table 2): (i) complete mediation. **Illustrative cases.** Gemini CLI, GitLab Duo, Clinejection.

**On GitHub Actions.** Native: A new virtual machine for each job on GitHub-hosted runners. Gap and compensating control: No native egress allow-list; use self-hosted ephemeral runners with network policy, or a runtime monitor.

**New relative to existing standards.** Default-deny egress for agents.

**In this repository.** Templates: `obaaf-agent-propose.yml: cache-mode none, no persisted credentials, optional egress monitor` · Checker rules: `OBAAF-GHA-006`, `OBAAF-GHA-007`, `OBAAF-GHA-011`, `OBAAF-GHA-013`, `OBAAF-GHA-020`

### R8 Attest every agent run

**Requirement.** Each invocation produces a signed attestation. It binds the triggering event and principal; the digests and labels of the input snapshot (R1); the granted authority and identity (R2, R3); the versions of the agent, harness, and model (R6); the digests of the proposals produced; and any approvals (R4). Fields describing inputs, authority, and outputs are generated by jobs the agent cannot influence. The agent's self-reported trace of tool calls is recorded but marked untrusted. Release verification checks that every change made through the agent path carries an attestation.

**Why.** R8 addresses RC3 and gives auditors a record of what each agent saw, could do, and did.

**Root causes.** RC3. **Assumption secured** (Paper 1, Table 2): Detection and audit. **Illustrative cases.** Amazon Q, Nx.

**On GitHub Actions.** Native: The attest action with custom predicates. Gap and compensating control: Agent-specific fields are project-defined.

**New relative to existing standards.** An agent-run predicate.

**In this repository.** Tools: `obaaf attest agent-run`, `obaaf verify agent-run`, `obaaf attest approval`, `obaaf verify release` · Templates: `obaaf-agent-propose.yml: attest job`, `obaaf-agent-apply.yml`, `obaaf-publish.yml: verify jobs` · Schemas: `agent-run.schema.json`, `agent-approval.schema.json` · Checker rules: `OBAAF-GHA-016`, `OBAAF-GHA-021`

## The agent-run record

Each agent run produces a signed in-toto attestation. Fields the agent could influence are kept apart and marked untrusted. See [the attestation formats](../docs/attestations.md).

| Field | Content | Produced by | Trusted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Subject | Digests of the proposal bundle files | Attestation step | Yes |
| Trigger | Event type and identifier, repository, triggering principal and level | Snapshot step | Yes |
| Inputs | Each snapshot item with digest, channel, and label; the computed integrity level | Snapshot step | Yes |
| Authority | Token permissions, names of secrets granted, network policy, OIDC permission | Protected workflow definition and snapshot step | Yes |
| Agent | Digests of the action and harness; model identifier and version as reported by the inference proxy | Snapshot step and proxy | Yes |
| Trace | Tool calls with digests of their arguments | Agent harness | No (self-reported) |
| Approvals | Reviewer identity, time, and environment | Effect lane | Yes |

*How version 0.1 differs from Paper 1, Table 3.* The Trace field holds one digest of the agent's trace file, not a digest per tool call. The approval time is when the effect lane read the approval, because GitHub's approvals API returns no review time. The model identifier and version stay empty until an inference proxy reports them (version 0.2, DECISIONS.md D-020). Models are therefore not yet pinned by digest (FR10).

## Documented incidents

Under the assumptions of Paper 1, section 5.3, the requirements would have prevented (P) or contained (C) the harmful outcome in each case.

| Case | Disclosed | Status | Root causes | Prevented by | Contained by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Rules File Backdoor | 2025-03 | Demonstrated | RC1, RC3 | R5 (if the file entered through review) | R4, R8 |
| GitHub MCP | 2025-05 | Demonstrated | RC1, RC2 | R2 | R1, R3 |
| GitLab Duo | 2025-05 | Demonstrated | RC1, RC2 | R2 | R7 |
| Gemini CLI | 2025-07 | Demonstrated | RC1, RC2 | - | R2, R7 |
| Amazon Q extension | 2025-07 | Exploited | RC2, RC3 | R3, R4, R5 | R8 |
| Nx "s1ngularity" | 2025-08 | Exploited | RC1, RC2, RC3 | R1, R2, R3, R4 | R8 |
| CamoLeak | 2025-10 | Demonstrated | RC1, RC2 | R2 | R7 |
| PromptPwnd | 2025-12 | Demonstrated | RC1, RC2 | R2, R3 | R4, R7 |
| Claude Code action | 2026-02 | Demonstrated | RC1, RC2 | R1 | R2 |
| Clinejection | 2026-02 | Exploited | RC1, RC2, RC3 | R7 | R2, R3, R8 |
